scores.evidence: The app features high ad density without a path for users to earn a cleaner reading experience through a value exchange. The reward is '15 minutes of ad-free reading' directly addressing this pain point. The trigger is in the core news feed after two articles, a common moment of engagement.

The proposal adds a new, desirable 'Ad-free Sprint' experience without removing existing free value. The integration includes a clear offer card and a countdown timer badge, making the feature intuitive and enhancing the user experience during the sprint. The 'AOL' Game Partner is in-world.

The reward is strictly time-boxed (15 minutes) and capped (3 per day) for 'Non-paying users'. The digest states 'No priced packs observed' and no paid ad-free subscriptions exist, which effectively eliminates direct cannibalization risk.

The computed 'Cost to serve per view' is $0.0000, meaning the net revenue per view is 100% of the gross ($0.0090–$0.0150). The reward is an ad-free experience, not a directly priced resource, so COGS is negligible.

The trigger is 'A promotional card appears in the Home News Feed after the user scrolls past the first two articles' on screen 's02 (Home News Feed)', which is a 'core-loop' surface with 'frequent' visits, ensuring high visibility and frequent opportunities.

The proposal leverages a standard 'SIM-RWD' unit, grants on 'REWARD_VERIFIED', and involves new UI elements like a feed card and a timer, which are straightforward to implement. The 'Ad-free Sprint' is a common time-boxed entitlement mechanic.

Uses 'AOL' as the Game Partner and directly targets existing 'Taboola ads' and 'banner advertisements' on 'news feeds and article pages' specific to the app's content. The 'Ad-Free Sprint' is tailored to AOL's ad-heavy experience.
The proposal includes explicit caps: 'perDay: 3' and 'cooldownMin: 60'. It also acknowledges the risk of a 'JARring return to ads' but does not specify a mitigation for this transition.

The proposal clearly defines a 'primary: Ad-free Sprint sessions started' metric, relevant 'guardrails' (news reading time, retention, ad impressions), and a 'User-level holdout, 10% share, 28 days' for a robust experiment.

requiredChanges: Verify and explicitly describe how all existing ad elements (native, banner) across all relevant screens will be suppressed during the Ad-free Sprint, beyond just e47 as shown in the storyboard.
Propose a small UX mitigation for the 'JARring return to ads' risk at the end of the 15-minute session (e.g., a subtle fade-in or a brief notification).
Consider a more specific character name for the 'Game Partner' than just 'AOL' to enhance specificity and in-world narrative.
